topics.label: Introduction and Course Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory welcome, lecture framing, and learning outcomes for the cancer biology module.

topics.label: Cancer as a Breakdown in Differentiation and Tissue Organization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a failure of regulated developmental programs and tissue architecture resulting from accumulated genetic changes, while considering how these cellular behaviors are modeled in the laboratory.

topics.label: Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tumors transition from localized benign growths to invasive and metastatic malignancies, using histological criteria and the adenoma-carcinoma sequence as a model.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the standard terminology and clinical naming conventions used to categorize benign and malignant neoplasms across different tissue lineages.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Cancer Pathogenesis and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical and systemic mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors impair normal organ function and lead to patient morbidity and death.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence Across Human Populations and Animal Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological distribution of tumor types in humans and examine comparative cancer incidence across multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Clinical Applications of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the rationale, diagnostic criteria, and clinical trade-offs of population screening strategies designed to detect pre-malignant lesions across various organs.

topics.label: Conclusion and Practical Reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary review of learning outcomes and practical session announcements.
